title: Main Errors in Articles on Regulator Design
content: In the process of reviewing our papers on controller design methods, we very often encounter reviewers' demands that are almost never met in most papers in this area. Our responses to reviewers with explanations do not always convince them. In this regard, several papers describing our results in this area have been rejected by reviewers, or we have been forced to make so many corrections to them that in many cases the essence of the paper is partially lost. At the same time, in each paper we have to explain anew what should be clear to a specialist in automatic control theory, otherwise he cannot be considered a specialist in this area. The most surprising thing is that we often encounter published papers that contain such gross errors or inconsistencies that one can only wonder how two or three reviewers and the editor-in-chief could accept such papers for publication. We analyze one such example of a paper that should not have been published under any circumstances. But the problem is not this article, but a large number of similar articles that also should not have been published.
